Sample Question: Why is the focal length of a plane mirror infinite? Explain what it means that the focal point is to be at infinity. 14.6 Application of Spherical Mirrors Concave mirror i. A concave mirror in reflecting type astronomical telescopes of large aperture: A concave mirror is used in reflecting type astronomical telescopes of large aperture because a lens of a very large aperture, and free from various defects cannot be obtained in practice. ii. A concave mirror for shaving: A concave mirror is preferred to a plane mirror for shaving because when a person keeps his face between the pole and the focus of the concave mirror, an erected and highly magnified virtual image is formed. As a result, a proper close shaving will be possible. iii. A concave mirror in the ophthalmoscope: The concave mirror is used in ophthalmoscope so that by looking through the hole at the centre of the concave mirror, doctors can examine the eyes in a proper way. iv. The concave mirror as reflector: Concave mirrors are used as reflectors in cinema projectors, magic lanterns, etc. Also, the concave parabolic mirrors are used in searchlights. Convex mirror in vehicles for rear view: A convex mirror is used in vehicles for rear view. The objects behind the vehicle are in front of the convex mirror so that the virtual, erected and diminished images are produced between the pole and the focus. This gives the clear view of the most of the rear objects to the driver. Thus, a convex mirror provides a much wider field of view; however, it cannot give the exact idea about the distance and speed of the approaching vehicle.
